To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) plant growth and development should be controlled to avoid premature exposure to inductive conditions, (ii) the reduction of temperature during flower induction does not affect flowering earlieness and stem quality, and (iii) supplemental lighting promotes flowering earlieness, stem branching, and the emission of the secondary stems, compared to the standard light regime.

(i) the reduction of the plant size at the beginning of the phase of flower initiation does not affect the flowering earliness and quality, and (ii) the reduction of light intensity and temperature during the phase of flowering induction does not affect the earliness of flowering and quality of flower stems, but it promotes the stem branching.

(i) plant exposure to inductive conditions before attaining a minimum critical size delays flowering and reduces the quality of flower stems; (ii) a moderate reduction of temperature does not affect flowering and quality of flower stems, but it promotes stem branching; (iii) a moderate increase of light intensity promotes flowering and the emission of the first flower stem, and it also promotes stem branching.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of new strategies for the optimization of the thermal and photoperiodic environment in Mediterranean greenhouses, to improve the commercial quality of flower crops of Phalaenopis hybrids.

the optimization of the inductive treatment of Phalaenopisis hybrids, in order to obtain a higher commercial quality of flower stem and a higher number of flower stems per plant, and a higher earliness of flowering.

the development of a new strategy for the production of Phalaenopssis hybrids in Mediterranean greenhouses, in which the inductive phase is postponed to the end of the juvenile phase, when the plants reach the critical size for the onset of flowering.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a moderate reduction of temperature and an adequate light intensity during flower induction, are useful to reduce the production costs of Phalaenopis hybrids in Mediterranean greenhouses.

the reduction of plant size, the lowering of the temperature, and the supplemental lighting, in the phase of flower initiation, can reduce the thermal requirements and anticipate flowering, but they can also reduce the quality of flower stems.

the flowering of Phalaenopsisis influenced by a combination of factors, including plant size, temperature and light intensity, which should be carefully considered for a successful production in Mediterranean greenhouses.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the plant size, temperature and light intensity, in the phase of flowering induction, affect flowering of modern Phalaenopsis hybrids in Mediterranean greenhouses.
, to reduce the thermal requirements of Phalaenopsishybrids, the plants should be kept in a juvenile phase for as long as possible, to allow them to reach the optimal size for flowering.

a reduced plant size and temperature, and a lower light intensity during flower induction, can be used in Mediterranean greenhouses to improve the flowering performance of modern Phalaenopsis hybrids.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the inductive treatments, which are commonly adopted in tropical countries, are not effective for the modern hybrids of Phalaenopsisspecifically selected for Mediterranean greenhouse cultivation.
the inductive treatments, in the Mediterranean greenhouses for Phalaenopsis cultivation, must be applied when plants reach the critical size, to obtain a high commercial quality of flowering.

, in Mediterranean greenhouses, the use of smaller plants and a reduction of temperature and light intensity during the phase of induction of flowering, can reduce the thermal requirements and the production costs, with no negative effects on flower stem quality.
